source.title: Circuits in Superposition 2: Now with Less Wrong Math

record.tranche_reason: The post develops a theoretical construction for computation in superposition and reports preliminary results about sparse circuit-to-neuron connectivity. It does not test the claim versions' specified representational geometry, capacity account, LLM evidence, SAE features, or feature dimensionality.
record.gate_note: The post reports preliminary toy-model observations about circuit connectivity, recorded below as a related finding that fits no version. Its GPT-2 activation-rate figure is cited rather than measured here; the post's theoretical calculations concern its proposed construction, not an empirical test of the listed claim versions.
record.test_reason: The post is a theoretical construction for computation in superposition across multiple MLP layers, with error-propagation bounds. It reports no measurement of feature geometry, capacity allocation, polysemanticity causes, LLM features, SAE features or feature dimensionality. The only empirical content is a preliminary, unquantified toy experiment on circuit-to-neuron connectivity, which concerns a different construct (sparse circuit wiring under noise). The GPT-2 ~20% activation rate is cited, not measured.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also conclude that the number of circuits that fit scales with parameter count (roughly D^2/(z^2 d^2)). Computation capacity is far below storage capacity, and noise suppression is necessary. They do not predict sparse neuron activations overall, but they do tentatively predict sparse circuit-to-neuron use. The toy evidence for that prediction is weak and still in progress.
record.recipe_differences: The post presents a mathematical construction for embedding small multilayer circuits in a larger MLP; it does not reproduce the original toy-model feature-storage method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported toy-model connectivity result differed between the one-layer setup without added input noise and the setup with added input noise.

fits_no_version.finding: In preliminary toy models, one-layer training without input noise gave no sparse circuit-to-neuron connectivity. Adding input noise, to simulate deeper layers, did yield sparse connectivity. No numbers are reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Networks doing multi-layer computation in superposition connect each circuit to only a small fraction of neurons, to suppress interference noise.

fits_no_version.finding: The theoretical construction implies a computation capacity of roughly D^2/(z^2 d^2) circuits, versus storage capacity exponential in D. Interference noise first dominates at layer 2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Capacity for computation in superposition scales quadratically with width, while storage capacity scales exponentially; single-layer toy models miss the dominant noise term.

record.problems: The toy-model experiment is described as preliminary and still in progress. No numerical outcomes, uncertainty estimates, or experimental controls are reported. The author notes that the models used L2 loss, which may be unsuitable for incentivising superposition.

untested.parts: No test of overlapping, nearly orthogonal feature storage, a sparsity transition, or geometry. The storage-capacity formula is derived from cited work, not tested.
No test of importance-based dedicated versus shared dimensions.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.
No LLM feature-distribution or SAE measurement. The GPT-2 activation rate is cited only.
The construction embeds d-dimensional circuits but does not test the dimensionality of features in models.

record.verdict_notes: The post is theoretical and has no peer review. The Colab code builds the embedding matrices, not the toy experiments. The reader's relation (discusses) and tranche (T6) are accepted.

versions.untested_parts: The post does not test whether sparse features are represented as overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions, or whether their geometry changes with sparsity.
The post does not test whether feature importance and capacity competition lead to dedicated or shared dimensions.
The post does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.
The post does not measure feature distributions or dictionary recovery in LLMs.
The post does not evaluate whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical.
The post does not test whether represented features are one-dimensional directions.

rows.subject: toy models of superposition

rows.note: The author says these models had only one computational layer. The post also says they were trained with L2 loss, which the author considers probably unsuitable for incentivising superposition.
